history.p:
‘Artaban’ was Scheibe’s first opera or ‘Singspiel’ composed while he lived in Hamburg in 1738. Around this time Scheibe was very interested in promoting German opera, and in the foreword to the libretto he concludes that the opera is a 'a new German "Singspiel". [...] Everything that only gives such plays a good reputation has been observed in the preparation of the work. As well as being the first German piece in several years specifically written for our stage, so we promise ourselves so much the more an overall applause' (sig. )(3r). It was to have been staged at the Gänsemarkt-Oper in the early spring of 1738, but due to financial difficulties the opera company closed and ‘Artaban’ was cancelled. The planning had advanced to the stage that even the libretto had been published and is today the only source to Scheibe’s opera.
In his Critischer Musikus, 1737–40 (SchW C1:008), Scheibe mentions that he had been encouraged by friends to write a German opera and describes in detail what happened at the opera house in connection with the staging of the work. Scheibe was aware of the appalling and scandalous conditions in terms of stage, the performers as well as the directors, and it therefore took a long time for his friends to persuade him to compose the opera. When the conditions improved, Scheibe started on composing a draft based on a text by a young up-coming poet (the name of the poet remained a secret – was it possibly Scheibe himself?). However, his hands were bound, partly because of the staging and partly due to Marie Monza who, though she was one of the best on the stage, could not sing in German. This is also evident in the libretto, for the arias which she was to have sung were indeed in Italian; it should be noted, however, that Monza's recitatives are in German. Scheibe mentions in the introduction that 'such a variation is, however, often more pleasant than when everything is sung in German' (sig. )(3r). The day of the premiere was set, but the opera was barely finished when one of the singers was ordered to travel to a foreign court while another singer became ill. Replacements were found, yet the progress was apparently a disaster including intrigues among the singers. At the preview the whole orchestra and all the singers except one were present; the missing singer did not turn up and did not wish to sing the part. All hopes for presenting a new German opera vanished and the director, Bartholomäus Monza, refused to pay Scheibe the fee. The Gänsemarkt-Oper was closed on 9 April 1738. According to one of Scheibe’s critics, Lorenz Christoph Mizler, the reason for why the opera was not performed was because 'the opera recently set in music is so contrived that it could barely be sung and played' (see Mizler (1738), p. 81). Though the opera was not performed in Hamburg, it seems that it was indeed performed ‘recently’ (that is, before February 1740) at some court for connoisseurs (Critischer Musikus, p. 708; SchW C1:008). One of the great admirers and patronisers of the Gänsemarkt-Oper in Hamburg was Bendix von Ahlefelt, a member of the Danish council and ‘Landesrath’ of Schleswig-Holstein who had amassed a vast collection of ‘Singspiele’ librettos while in Hamburg. It is possible that von Ahlefeldt was the instigator of the performance of ‘Artaban’.
Scheibe's interest in creating a German opera remained, and in 1749 while he lived in Copenhagen he published a libretto to another opera titled 'Thusnelde' (SchW B1:002).

annot.p:
Der Tempel des Sieges eröfnet sich. Er ist mit Palmenzweigen und mit Blumen ausgezieret. Die Priester gehen dem Könige entgegen, welcher auf einen Triumphwagen kommt, der von Sechs medischen Sclaven gezogen wird. Vor dem Wagen her, gehen viele Soldaten mit Siegeszeichen, eroberten Fahnen und Waffen. Hinter dem Wagen folgen eine Menge medische Sclaven, worunter man die Prinzeßin Barsine und ihren Bruder den Prinzen Tigranes erblicket. Diesen Aufzug beschliessen die Soldaten und eine Menge Volks. Der König steigt von dem Wagen und gehet zum Altar. Die Siegeszeichen, die eroberten Fahnen und Waffen werden in dem Tempel gehangen.
Phraates, Artaban, Tigranes, Barsine, die Vorigen.

annot.p: Der Tempel des Krigesgottes. Am Ende des Tempels stehet die Bildsäule des Kriegesgottes in einer fürchterlichen Gestalt. Auf dem Altare, welcher ganz blutig ist, brennet ein beständiges Feuer. Zur rechten Seite stehet eine prächtig ausgezierte Bühne für den König, zur linken Seite aber befinden sich die Priester. Am Altare stehet der Opferpriester, welcher ein großes Opfermesser in der Hand hält. Unter einer traurigen Music bringen die Soldaten die drey Verurtheilten, welche ganz weiß gekleidet, und auf den Häuptern mit Blumenkränzen gezieret sind. Sie werden den Priestern übergeben, und zum Altare geführet. Artaban, Barsine, Tigranes, hernach Mandane.
